screening.reason: Inclusion 2,3: resting-state fMRI diagnostic classification (ASD vs HC) analysis using ABIDE I data with a graph attention network model.

evidence_spans.text: We experimentally compared GAT2 model’s performance on the  ABIDE I database from 1035 subjects
We used the resting-state fMRI data from 1035 subjects in the ABIDE I initiative [20]  for this study. The dataset includes 505 individuals diagnosed as having ASD and 530  HC.
evidence_spans.claim: Final analysed cohort: 505 ASD, 530 HC from ABIDE I.

evidence_spans.text: The data were preprocessed by the Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Con- nectomes (CPAC) pipeline [24] that included the following procedure: slice timing cor- rection, motion realignment, intensity normalization, regression of nuisance signals,  band-pass filtering (0.01–0.1 Hz) and registration of fMRI images to standard anatomi- cal space (MNI152).
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing done with the CPAC pipeline from the Preprocessed Connectomes Project.

evidence_spans.text: We use the Harvard Oxford (HO) atlas [23], so we  have N = 110 nodes.
evidence_spans.claim: Primary parcellation is the Harvard-Oxford atlas (110 ROIs); AAL atlas used for comparison.

evidence_spans.text: After randomly perform- ing fivefold cross-validation data division, in each round of experiments, one-fold data    Page 11 of 20 Hu et al. BMC Bioinformatics          (2021) 22:379  	 were used for testing while other fourfold data were used for t
evidence_spans.claim: Evaluation used random fivefold cross-validation (no leave-site-out).

evidence_spans.text: The GAT2 model achieved the best results in accuracy, sensitivity, F1 score, and MCC  indicators using fivefold cross-validation, with the accuracy of 68.02%, sensitivity of  74.06%, F1 score of 69.31%, and MCC of 0.3426.
evidence_spans.claim: Main predictive performance: GAT2 best model, accuracy 68.02%, sensitivity 74.06%, F1 69.31%, MCC 0.3426.

evidence_spans.text: Compared  with the AAL atlas, using the HO atlas for construction of the brain network,  with the same model, the accuracy was increased by about 5%, the sensitivity was  increased by about 2%, and the F1 value was increas
evidence_spans.claim: Atlas choice affects classification performance: HO atlas outperforms AAL atlas.

evidence_spans.text: 3 rsFCs (the connection 4, 5, and 7) were statistically significant (p < 0.05)  between the ASD and HC groups.
evidence_spans.claim: Post-hoc interpretation identified 3 of 10 top connections with uncorrected group differences (p<0.05).

evidence_spans.text: The datasets analyzed during the current study are available in the ABIDE Preprocessed Connectomes Project website of  http://​prepr​ocess​ed-​conne​ctomes-​proje​ct.​org/​abide/​downl​oad.​html. The source codes of GAT-LI are publicly available  at the project website of https://​github.​com/​large​app/​gat-​li.
evidence_spans.claim: Data source and analysis code are publicly released.

assessments.support: N (505 ASD/530 HC from 1035 ABIDE I subjects) is stated, but no explicit QC/motion exclusion rule for arriving at this 1035 subset is reported in the text.
"The data were preprocessed by the Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Con- nectomes (CPAC) pipeline" and Harvard-Oxford/AAL atlases both specified with node counts.
"The dataset includes 505 individuals diagnosed as having ASD and 530  HC" — diagnostic label taken directly from the ABIDE I phenotype file (standard site clinical diagnosis).

Evaluation used pooled random fivefold cross-validation with no leave-site-out scheme and no site covariate/harmonisation reported; interpretation-stage connection differences (Table 6) reported as uncorrected p<0.05 with no multiple-comparison correction.

risk_of_bias.summary: Pipeline, atlas and labels are clearly reported, but site is not modelled or held out in cross-validation and the post-hoc connection-level comparisons are uncorrected for multiple comparisons, per PROBAST Analysis domain criteria.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction study; ABIDE I, 1035 subjects (505 ASD, 530 HC), pooled across all contributing sites
narrative_row.methods: CPAC-preprocessed resting-state functional connectivity (Harvard-Oxford atlas, 110 ROIs) classified with a novel graph attention network (GAT2) within a graph-learning-and-interpreting framework (GAT-LI); compared against SVM, RF, MLP, CNN and other GNN baselines using fivefold cross-validation
narrative_row.outcomes: GAT2 achieved the best classification performance among compared models (accuracy 68.02%, sensitivity 74.06%, F1 69.31%, MCC 0.3426 with the HO atlas); GNNExplainer-based interpretation identified a set of discriminative functional connections, 3 of which showed uncorrected group differences (p<0.05)
narrative_row.key_limitations: No leave-site-out or site-covariate evaluation despite multi-site data; no motion/QC rule reported for the analysed subset; post-hoc connection-level tests uncorrected for multiple comparisons
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Full ABIDE I 1035-subject PCP release used with CPAC/HO atlas; code and data source publicly linked, supporting reconstructibility of the pipeline though not an explicit subject-selection rule.

evidence_quotes: We used the resting-state fMRI data from 1035 subjects in the ABIDE I initiative [20]  for this study. The dataset includes 505 individuals diagnosed as having ASD and 530  HC.

The GAT2 model achieved the best results in accuracy, sensitivity, F1 score, and MCC  indicators using fivefold cross-validation, with the accuracy of 68.02%, sensitivity of  74.06%, F1 score of 69.31%, and MCC of 0.3426.

The datasets analyzed during the current study are available in the ABIDE Preprocessed Connectomes Project website of  http://​prepr​ocess​ed-​conne​ctomes-​proje​ct.​org/​abide/​downl​oad.​html. The source codes of GAT-LI are publicly available  at the project website of https://​github.​com/​large​app/​gat-​li.
